conceptual assets.concept: Control register configuration (enable and IRQ mask bits)
conceptual assets.reasoning: The bus_access process initializes and stores control bits in the local ctrl record on reset and on bus writes: reset clears them (`if (rstn_i = '0') then ctrl.enable <= '0'; ...`), and on a write when bus_req_i.stb and bus_req_i.rw='1' and bus_req_i.addr(2)='0' the process assigns `ctrl.enable <= bus_req_i.data(ctrl_en_c)` and the irq_* fields from bus_req_i.data. The same ctrl fields are read back into bus_rsp_o.data and are used by irq_generator to compute irq_o. The RTL therefore establishes stored configuration values whose corruption would violate the implemented control/IRQ behavior.

The irq_generator process drives irq_o from ctrl.enable and the configured irq mask bits combined with FIFO status signals: `irq_o <= ctrl.enable and ((ctrl.irq_rx_avail and rx_fifo.avail) or ... or (ctrl.irq_tx_nhalf and (not tx_fifo.half)));`. The RTL therefore defines irq_o as the module's reported interrupt event; corruption of this output would change the implemented IRQ behavior.

conceptual assets.concept: Synchronized SDI input signals (sck, csn, sdi) used to control transfers
conceptual assets.reasoning: The synchronizer process samples external lines into flip-flops and the RTL computes synchronized signals (`sync.sck <= sync.sck_ff(1) xor sync.sck_ff(2);`, `sync.csn <= sync.csn_ff(1);`, `sync.sdi <= sync.sdi_ff(1);`). serial_engine uses sync.csn, sync.sck and sync.sdi in its state transitions and bit sampling (`if (sync.csn = '0') then serial.start <= '1';`, `elsif (sync.sck = '1') then ... serial.sreg <= ... & serial.sdi_ff;`). The computed synchronized inputs are therefore decision inputs the module depends on; their integrity is established by the RTL.

conceptual assets.concept: Serial transfer byte register (serial.sreg) — the active transmit/receive byte
conceptual assets.reasoning: serial.sreg is loaded and updated by serial_engine (`serial.sreg <= tx_fifo.rdata` or `serial.sreg <= (others => '0')` in state "100"; while shifting `serial.sreg <= serial.sreg(serial.sreg'left-1 downto 0) & serial.sdi_ff` in state "111"); serial.done then causes `rx_fifo.wdata <= serial.sreg`. serial.sreg therefore holds the byte being shifted out or the byte received and written into RX FIFO; the RTL establishes it as the in-module representation of transfer data whose integrity matters.

conceptual assets.concept: SDI serial output bit (sdi_dat_o) — bit leaving the module
conceptual assets.reasoning: The RTL assigns the physical SDI output from the shift register MSB: `sdi_dat_o <= serial.sreg(serial.sreg'left);`. sdi_dat_o is therefore the port through which serialized data leaves the entity; the RTL establishes its value and relation to serial.sreg, so its integrity is primary.

conceptual assets.concept: Received byte available to the CPU (RX FIFO content)
conceptual assets.reasoning: The RTL captures completed serial bytes into the RX FIFO (`rx_fifo.wdata <= serial.sreg;` and `rx_fifo.we <= serial.done;`) and provides the stored byte to bus reads (`bus_access` assigns `bus_rsp_o.data(7 downto 0) <= rx_fifo.rdata` when reading FIFO). The module therefore defines rx_fifo.rdata as the stored receive-byte value accessible to bus reads; its integrity is established by these assignments.

conceptual assets.concept: RX FIFO occupancy/status signals (avail, half, free)
conceptual assets.reasoning: bus_access reads RX FIFO status into readback words (`bus_rsp_o.data(ctrl_rx_avail_c) <= rx_fifo.avail;`, `bus_rsp_o.data(ctrl_rx_half_c) <= rx_fifo.half;`, `bus_rsp_o.data(ctrl_rx_full_c) <= not rx_fifo.free;`) and irq_generator uses these flags in irq conditions (`(ctrl.irq_rx_avail and rx_fifo.avail) or (ctrl.irq_rx_half and rx_fifo.half) or (ctrl.irq_rx_full and (not rx_fifo.free))`). The RTL therefore establishes these status signals as module-observed FIFO occupancy indicators whose integrity affects status readback and IRQs.

conceptual assets.concept: TX FIFO byte (data to be transmitted)
conceptual assets.reasoning: The module sources TX data from bus writes into the TX FIFO (`tx_fifo.wdata <= bus_req_i.data(7 downto 0);` with tx_fifo.we set on bus writes) and serial_engine loads transmit data from the FIFO into the shift register (`if (tx_fifo.avail = '0') then serial.sreg <= (others => '0') else serial.sreg <= tx_fifo.rdata;`). The RTL thus defines tx_fifo.wdata and tx_fifo.rdata as the module's transmitted-byte interfaces; their integrity is established by these assignments and uses.

conceptual assets.concept: TX FIFO occupancy/status signals (avail, half, free)
conceptual assets.reasoning: bus_access reports TX status (`bus_rsp_o.data(ctrl_tx_empty_c) <= not tx_fifo.avail;`, `bus_rsp_o.data(ctrl_tx_nhalf_c) <= not tx_fifo.half;`, `bus_rsp_o.data(ctrl_tx_full_c) <= not tx_fifo.free;`) and irq_generator uses these signals in IRQ conditions (`ctrl.irq_tx_empty and (not tx_fifo.avail)` or `ctrl.irq_tx_nhalf and (not tx_fifo.half)`). The RTL therefore establishes these TX status signals as observable module state whose integrity affects status readback and IRQs.

conceptual assets.concept: Bus-driven FIFO access decisions (tx write enable and rx read enable)
conceptual assets.reasoning: The RTL computes control signals that gate bus transactions into/from the FIFOs: `tx_fifo.we <= '1' when (bus_req_i.stb = '1') and (bus_req_i.rw = '1') and (bus_req_i.addr(2) = '1') else '0';` and `rx_fifo.re <= '1' when (bus_req_i.stb = '1') and (bus_req_i.rw = '0') and (bus_req_i.addr(2) = '1') else '0';`. These computed signals determine whether a bus write pushes into TX FIFO or a bus read pulls from RX FIFO; the RTL therefore establishes them as decision points whose integrity matters.

conceptual assets.concept: Transfer start decision (serial.start) that triggers a transmit sequence
conceptual assets.reasoning: serial.start is asserted by serial_engine when the module is enabled and CS becomes active (`when "100": if (sync.csn = '0') then serial.start <= '1'; end if;`); tx_fifo.re is driven from serial.start (`tx_fifo.re <= serial.start;`) so serial.start is the RTL-established trigger that initiates reading TX data and starting a serial transfer. The RTL therefore establishes serial.start as a stored decision whose integrity affects whether a transfer begins.
